name: Simple Lentil Soup
pitch: With just lentils and tomatoes already on hand, this humble soup is exactly the kind of thing that makes you feel like you've got it together on a weeknight.
timeEstimate: ~55 min (or 20 min with a pressure cooker)
steps: Rinse your lentils well under cold water, then let them soak in lukewarm water for 20–30 minutes if you have time — it helps them cook more evenly, though you can skip it if you're in a rush.
Chop your tomatoes roughly and toss them into a saucepan with the lentils. If you have an onion, halve it and throw it in — it adds a lot of flavor. Garlic is great here too if you have it.
Cover everything with water (about 4–5 cups), add a pinch of salt and pepper, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 45 minutes to an hour until the lentils are soft and creamy.
Taste and adjust salt. A small splash of vinegar or lemon juice at the end brightens the whole thing up — totally optional but worth it if you have either on hand.
Serve as-is, or with some crusty bread if you've got it.

name: Ethiopian-Style Lentil Curry
pitch: This is a deeply warming, hearty curry — and honestly, even a simplified version with whatever spices you have in the cupboard is really satisfying.
steps: Heat a glug of oil in a large pot over medium heat. If you have an onion, dice it and cook until soft and golden, about 8 minutes — this is the flavor base, so don't rush it.
Add garlic if you have it (2–3 cloves, minced or just roughly chopped). Cook for another minute until fragrant.

Add your lentils and stir them around for a couple of minutes. Now's the time to add whatever spices you have — cumin, curry powder, chili flakes, smoked paprika all work well here. The recipe calls for amchar masala and masala molida, but a teaspoon each of cumin and curry powder is a totally solid substitute.
Pour in your canned or chopped tomatoes plus a squeeze of tomato paste if you have it. Add about 2 cups of water and stir everything together.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer on low for about an hour until the lentils are completely tender. Check occasionally and add a splash more water if it's getting too thick.
If you have plain yogurt, stir a dollop in right at the end — it makes it creamy and cools the heat a little. Serve over rice or with flatbread if you have either.

name: Spiced Red Lentil & Tomato Soup
pitch: Lentils and tomatoes are a classic pairing that come together into a hearty, warming soup with just pantry spices doing the heavy lifting.
steps: Heat a drizzle of oil in a medium pot over medium heat. Add 2–3 minced garlic cloves and cook for about a minute until fragrant.
Stir in 1 tsp cumin, ½ tsp turmeric, and a pinch of chili flakes (or whatever warm spices you have), and let them toast for 30 seconds.
Add 1 cup of rinsed lentils and your chopped tomatoes (2–3 fresh or a can works great). Stir everything together.
Pour in about 3 cups of water, season generously with salt and pepper, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 20–25 minutes until the lentils are completely soft. Taste and adjust seasoning — a small splash of vinegar at the end brightens it up nicely.
Serve as-is for a rustic soup, or use an immersion blender to make it silky smooth. Simple but genuinely satisfying.
